s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with mental confusion and generalized weakness
salient_findings: Progressive mental confusion over two months
Two left occipital lesions with surrounding vasogenic edema on MRI
key_facts: Two-month history of progressive mental confusion
Marked worsening over the past two weeks
Complete dependence for basic activities of daily living
Regular contact with various birds, including pigeons
Able only to obey simple commands
Two left occipital lesions with surrounding vasogenic edema on MRI

shortlist.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive neurological decline with mental confusion and generalized weakness, and presence of brain lesions on MRI

shortlist.label: Glioblastoma multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of two left occipital lesions with surrounding vasogenic edema on MRI, consistent with a high-grade brain tumor

shortlist.label: Metastatic brain tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive neurological decline and presence of multiple brain lesions, which could be consistent with metastatic disease

shortlist.label: Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Contact with birds, which could be a source of Toxoplasma gondii infection, and presence of brain lesions on MRI

shortlist.label: Cysticercosis
shortlist.why_kept: Contact with birds and presence of brain lesions on MRI, which could be consistent with neurocysticercosis

raw.rationale: The patient's rapid decline and presence of two distinct lesions with surrounding vasogenic edema on MRI are more suggestive of metastatic disease, especially given the lack of other systemic abnormalities that might point to a primary brain tumor or infectious cause.

rejected.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a single lesion and more often associated with immunocompromised states

rejected.label: Glioblastoma multiforme
rejected.why: Usually presents with a single, heterogeneous lesion and less likely to cause such rapid decline without other focal deficits

rejected.label: Toxoplasmosis
rejected.why: More commonly seen in immunocompromised patients and would not typically cause such a rapid decline without other systemic signs

rejected.label: Cysticercosis
rejected.why: Would likely present with multiple lesions at different stages and more often associated with seizures or other focal neurological deficits
